title: Exhaustion precondition 'already ran its correction' is never pinned — the only guard test uses a terminal status
evidence:
+//// - Exhaustion (AD-7 — the rc3-7 mechanism goes LIVE here): a delivery failure / wrong-person on a row that already ran its correction
+////   terminalizes as unreachable + stamps referee_contact_invalid + audits
+// A terminal row cannot be exhausted (sticky terminals — 0 rows).
+  set_status(db, call_id, "objected")
+  let assert Ok(returned) =
+    rc_sql.exhaust_reference_call(
+      db,
+      call,
+      "unreachable",
+      "email_bounced",
+      json.null(),
+      "",
+    )
+  list.length(returned.rows) |> should.equal(0)
+  row_field(db, call_id, "status") |> should.equal(Some("objected"))
detail: The header claims exhaustion fires only after a correction cycle, but the only guard test uses terminal status 'objected', which any liveness guard rejects. A live queued row with correction_cycles=0 is never exercised, so a status-only SQL guard could wrongly exhaust first failures.
recommended_fix: Add a test calling exhaust_reference_call on a live queued row with correction_cycles=0 and asserting 0 rows, pinning the 'already ran its correction' precondition.

title: Negative control became vacuous: sentinel string can never appear in the payload
evidence:
-  string.contains(body, "larry@example.com") |> should.be_false
+  // RC4.3 note: the referee's CONTACT snapshot now legitimately rides the
+  // payload (the §7.7 take-over chips + §8.3 edit prefill need it) — the
+  // negative control moved to a still-internal marker (form_token is never
+  // selected by the detail read).
+  string.contains(body, "form_token_internal_sentinel") |> should.be_false
detail: The old assertion checked a real value (larry@example.com). The replacement checks a literal sentinel that no code path emits, so a real form_token leak in the detail payload would pass this test.
recommended_fix: Assert form_token is absent structurally (e.g. decode the payload and check the key), or fetch a known token and assert it is not in the body.

title: Corrected contact values are never pinned as the re-invite source after correction
evidence:
+  row_field(db, call_id, "corrected_email")
+  |> should.equal(Some("larry.byrne@example.com"))
+  row_field(db, call_id, "contact_email")
+  |> should.equal(Some("larry@example.com"))
+  let assert Ok(returned) =
+    rc_sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(db, "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z", 50)
+  // The employer row is still queued + due, so exactly ONE row comes back
+  // (the taken-over landlord row is excluded).
detail: Tests pin corrected_* holding the new email while contact_* keeps the old, and pin the sweep selecting by clock, but no test asserts the re-armed invite uses the corrected address; if it reads contact_* the correction is inert.
recommended_fix: Add an assertion that the sweep/invite step emits the corrected email (corrected_* or the updated app trio) for a corrected row.

+  set_status(db, call_id, "awaiting_correction")

detail: config, landlord, app and call are bound but never used; every request goes through correct_http, which rebuilds its own config. Gleam will warn on all four unused variables.
recommended_fix: Drop the unused bindings and the uuid assertions, or drive one request through do_correct so the bindings are exercised.

title: One-cycle rule relies solely on status; a cycles cap is never pinned
evidence:
+  // One cycle spent: the second correct on an already-corrected (queued)
+  // row also 409s — the awaiting guard IS the one-cycle rule (AD-7).
+  set_status(db, call_id, "awaiting_correction")
+  actions_handler.do_correct(config, app, landlord, vacancy, call, trio).status
+  |> should.equal(200)
+  actions_handler.do_correct(config, app, landlord, vacancy, call, trio).status
+  |> should.equal(409)
+  row_field(db, call_id, "correction_cycles") |> should.equal(Some("1"))
detail: The 409 after a second correct fires because the row left awaiting_correction, not because correction_cycles hit a cap. Nothing pins do_correct on an awaiting_correction row already at cycles=1 (set_status can create that state); the SQL would bump to 2.
recommended_fix: Add a test: set awaiting_correction on a row with cycles=1 and assert do_correct 409s or that cycles never exceeds 1.
